description: We are a technical duo (AI/Data & Full-stack/Hardware) building an AI/IoT platform for the 'Field Shift' challenge. Our coding is fully covered. We need a creative teammate to handle UI/UX design, storytelling, and the 3-minute pitch video. If you have an agriculture/business background and want to focus purely on design and presentation, join us!
summary:
Field Shift is an AI-powered agricultural digital twin designed to combat climate-induced crop failures and optimize global water usage. We developed an end-to-end pipeline that ingests real-time satellite data (NASA POWER, Earth Engine) and soil composition metrics (ISRIC SoilGrids) to calculate physics-informed features like the Vapor Pressure Deficit and Soil Sponge Index.

To address the challenge, our system utilizes an optimized CatBoost machine learning model to accurately predict root soil moisture and detect severe water stress. To ensure trustworthiness, we integrated a zero-hallucination Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) engine powered by Gemini and official FAO-56 guidelines. This translates complex predictive analytics into actionable, scientifically verified crop recommendations.

Field Shift is crucial because it democratizes advanced aerospace data. Featuring a bilingual (Arabic/English) interface and an interactive map, it empowers everyday farmers to make immediate, precise irrigation decisions, ultimately securing food production and conserving vital water resources in vulnerable regions.
details:
What it does & How it works Field Shift operates as a Space-to-Soil agricultural digital twin. The system begins by pinpointing a farm's exact location using a GPS-enabled interactive map. It automatically retrieves real-time climate data from NASA POWER and historical/satellite data from Google Earth Engine (MODIS NDVI/LST), alongside soil composition data from ISRIC SoilGrids. Rather than feeding raw data into an algorithm, we engineered physics-informed features, specifically the Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD) and our custom "Soil Sponge Index" (clay-to-sand ratio).

An optimized CatBoost regression model—trained on 100,000 temporal data points and rigorously validated using Spatial K-Fold cross-validation—calculates the optimal root soil moisture baseline. A deterministic decision engine compares this baseline to actual IoT sensor readings to detect water stress or over-irrigation. Finally, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) agent, powered by Gemini and grounded exclusively in FAO-56 irrigation guidelines via a local FAISS vector database, generates localized, zero-hallucination agricultural advice.

Benefits & Intended Impact The primary benefit is precision agriculture democratization. By identifying exact water deficits before visible crop stress occurs, Field Shift prevents crop failure and conserves vital freshwater resources. Its intended impact targets everyday farmers in vulnerable regions (starting with Egypt and the MENA region). The system translates complex aerospace and meteorological data into immediate, actionable advice in plain Arabic and English, completely removing the technical barrier to entry.


Tools, Coding Languages, & Software

  • Languages: Python
  • Data Pipeline: Google Earth Engine API, NASA POWER API, ISRIC SoilGrids REST API, Pandas, NumPy
  • Machine Learning: CatBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM, Scikit-learn (Voting Regressor, GroupKFold)
  • Generative AI & RAG: Google GenAI SDK (Gemini 3.8-flash), LangChain, FAISS, HuggingFace Sentence Transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
  • Frontend: Streamlit, Folium (Interactive Mapping)

Creativity & Factors Considered Our creativity lies in the Hybrid AI Architecture. We combined a deterministic JSON-based Rule Engine with a generative RAG system to achieve a "Zero-Hallucination" guarantee—a critical necessity in agriculture where wrong AI advice can destroy a harvest. We also factored in local constraints: the system includes a robust 503-error fallback mechanism for high-demand APIs, and the UI is fully responsive and localized (RTL Arabic support) to ensure it is immediately usable by local farmers on basic mobile devices
